North Warwickshire's population increased by around 3,000 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 65,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of North Warwickshire increased by 4.9%, from around 62,000 in 2011 to around 65,000 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the West Midlands (6.2%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, North Warwickshire was home to around 1.6 people per football pitch-sized piece of land. This area was among the lowest 25% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in North Warwickshire than across the West Midlands

An older North Warwickshire

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of North Warwickshire increased by two years, from 43 to 45 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the West Midlands as a whole in 2021 (40 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just over 1,400 (an increase of 10.7%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 2,400 (16.9% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.2 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Religion in North Warwickshire

In 2021, 38.1% of North Warwickshire residents reported having "No religion", up from 21.9% in 2011. The rise of 16.2 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in North Warwickshire. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 22.0% to 32.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 55.0% of people in North Warwickshire described themselves as Christian (down from 70.3%), while 5.0% did not state their religion (down from 6.4% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Marriage and civil partnership in North Warwickshire

North Warwickshire saw the West Midlands' second-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over who were married (or in a civil partnership) (from 51.8% in 2011 to 47.5% in 2021).

Across the region, only Dudley saw a greater fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were married (or in a civil partnership) (from 50.3% to 45.8%).

Every local authority area across the West Midlands saw a fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were married (or in a civil partnership), as the regional percentage fell from 47.7% to 45.3%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who were married or in a civil partnership in North Warwickshire decreased by 4.4 percentage points

Rise in private renting

In 2021, 14.9% of North Warwickshire households rented privately. This figure increased from 11.3% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in seven households (13.6%) lived in socially rented housing, compared with 14.4% in 2011. The percentage of North Warwickshire households that owned their home (outright or with a mortgage or loan) decreased from 72.4% to 70.4%.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes in North Warwickshire (3.6 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the West Midlands (3.9 percentage points, from 14.0% to 17.9%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Private renting in North Warwickshire increased by 3.6 percentage points

Unpaid care in North Warwickshire

In 2021, 4.7% of North Warwickshire residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.9%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.5% in 2011. The proportion of North Warwickshire residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care remained at 3.0%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in North Warwickshire (3.1 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the West Midlands (2.9 percentage points, from 7.4% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in North Warwickshire decreased by 3.1 percentage points

North Warwickshire residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 61,000 North Warwickshire residents said they were born in England. This represented 93.8% of the local population. The figure has risen from just over 58,800 in 2011, which at the time represented 94.9% of North Warwickshire's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with around 550 North Warwickshire residents reporting this country of birth (0.9%). This figure was down from around 650 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.1% of the population of North Warwickshire.

The number of North Warwickshire residents born in Romania rose from fewer than 50 in 2011 (0.0% of the local population) to just over 500 in 2021 (0.8%).

In 2021, 93.8% of North Warwickshire residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in North Warwickshire

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in nearby Nuneaton and Bedworth (3.1 percentage points) than in North Warwickshire (0.9 percentage points).

In North Warwickshire, the percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity increased from 1.6% in 2011 to 2.5% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Nuneaton and Bedworth increased from 3.6% to 6.7%.

The percentage of people who identified with a UK and non-UK national identity in North Warwickshire increased from 0.2% to 0.5%, while the percentage of people who identified as "British only" increased from 12.1% to 54.7%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in North Warwickshire increased by 0.9 percentage points

Fewer couples without children

Of North Warwickshire households, 18.8% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 20.8% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in six households (18.3%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 20.4% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children decreased from 8.5% to 8.2%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in North Warwickshire (2.0 percentage points) than across the West Midlands (1.0 percentage points, from 16.9% to 15.9%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in North Warwickshire decreased by 2.0 percentage points

Change in employment

Of North Warwickshire residents aged 16 years and over, 57.8% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 59.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 40 people (2.4%) said they were unemployed, compared with 3.3% in 2011. The percentage of retired North Warwickshire residents increased from 23.8% to 25.3%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in North Warwickshire (2.1 percentage points) than across the West Midlands (1.1 percentage points, from 54.4% to 53.3%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in North Warwickshire decreased by 2.1 percentage points

Fewer adults working long hours

North Warwickshire saw the West Midlands' joint second-largest percentage-point fall (alongside Stratford-on-Avon) in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week (from 14.5% in 2011 to 11.3% in 2021).

Across the region, only Malvern Hills saw a greater fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week (from 16.1% to 12.4%).

Every local authority area across the West Midlands saw a fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week, as the regional percentage fell from 12.1% to 10.1%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in North Warwickshire decreased by 3.2 percentage points

Disability in North Warwickshire

In 2021, 7.6% of North Warwickshire residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 9.6% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 10 people (10.2%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 10.0% in 2011. The proportion of North Warwickshire residents who were not disabled increased from 80.4% to 82.2%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in North Warwickshire (2.0 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the West Midlands (1.9 percentage points, from 9.9% to 8.0%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in North Warwickshire decreased by 2.0 percentage points

Health in North Warwickshire

In 2021, 47.0% of North Warwickshire residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 45.2% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.6% to 34.4%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of North Warwickshire residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.2% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 4.7% to 4.1%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in North Warwickshire increased by 1.8 percentage points

Ethnic groups in North Warwickshire

In 2021, 1.7% of North Warwickshire residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 0.8% in 2011. The 0.9 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 2.4% to 3.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 96.1% of people in North Warwickshire identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 97.9% in 2011), while 1.3% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 0.9% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 0.3% in 2011 to 0.6% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
